scenario: Two robotic inspection systems, RoboAlpha and RoboBeta, are compared on defect-detection accuracy across aged (>30 yr) and modern (<10 yr) reactor vessels. RoboAlpha is predominantly deployed in aged vessels; RoboBeta mostly in modern ones.

data.description: defect-detection accuracy rates by reactor age class and entity

question: (a) Which entity has the higher aggregate defect-detection accuracy rate? (b) Which entity performs better within each reactor age class stratum? (c) Compute each entity's corrected rate using a 50/50 reactor age class mix. (d) Which entity should be preferred, and why does the aggregate ranking mislead?

ground_truth.explanation: RoboBeta's higher aggregate is driven by its disproportionate assignment to easier modern <10 yr cases. RoboAlpha outperforms RoboBeta in both reactor age class strata. Standardising to a 50/50 reactor age class mix gives RoboAlpha 0.88 vs RoboBeta 0.84; RoboAlpha is the superior performer once reactor-age class is controlled.

naive_answer: RoboBeta is better because its aggregate defect-detection accuracy rate (0.9043) exceeds RoboAlpha's (0.83).
naive_trap: Reactor-age class is a confounder: RoboAlpha handles the majority of harder aged >30 yr cases, depressing its aggregate while RoboBeta benefits from easier cases.
reasoning_trace: (1) Aged >30 yr: RoboAlpha 0.81 > RoboBeta 0.75. (2) Modern <10 yr: RoboAlpha 0.95 > RoboBeta 0.93. (3) RoboAlpha handles 85.7% aged >30 yr cases vs RoboBeta's 14.3% — this pulls RoboAlpha's aggregate down. (4) Corrected 50/50: RoboAlpha=0.5×0.81+0.5×0.95=0.88; RoboBeta=0.5×0.75+0.5×0.93=0.84. RoboAlpha wins after standardisation.
python_verification:
nA1,rA1,nA2,rA2 = 600,0.81,100,0.95
nB1,rB1,nB2,rB2 = 100,0.75,600,0.93
ovA=(nA1*rA1+nA2*rA2)/(nA1+nA2); ovB=(nB1*rB1+nB2*rB2)/(nB1+nB2)
assert ovB > ovA, 'naive: RoboBeta aggregate higher'
cA=0.5*rA1+0.5*rA2; cB=0.5*rB1+0.5*rB2
assert abs(cA-0.88)<0.005 and abs(cB-0.84)<0.005
assert cA > cB, 'corrected: RoboAlpha wins'
